channelTitle: One hundred and thirty children followed the music - only three came back - Part 2
hook: In Part 1, the piper emptied Hamelin of rats - then, unpaid, he came back on a Sunday morning and played for the children instead.
storyParts: Out of the houses the children came, dancing behind the music - all the way to the side of a mountain that the old chronicle says opened up and closed behind them.
Only three children were left behind: one lame who could not keep up, one deaf who never heard the tune, and one blind who could not find the way - the town's whole future, gone in an hour.
Here is the strange part - the rat story was added centuries later. The oldest records only say the children vanished in 1284, with no rats mentioned at all.

Historians still argue what really happened: a mass emigration east, a children's crusade, or a dancing-sickness plague. Nobody found the children - but eastern towns recorded families with Hamelin names for generations.
In Hamelin today, the street where it happened still bans music and dancing out of respect - a seven-hundred-year-old town that never quite forgave itself.
cta: Which theory do you buy - plague, emigration, or something stranger? Grandma June wants your guess in the comments.
moral: A bargain broken by the powerful was paid for by the innocent - which is why the tale still stings.
seriesTitle: The Pied Piper - Grandma June Story Time
